exit: Explain Shall, Should, and May in your own words.
Name your security contacts (DITSO, security unit, ISIRT, line manager).
Say how you would report an incident without waiting to be certain.
State whether Tier 2/3 and App C might apply to a system you use.

items.text: Read S17 §1–2 and G3 §1–2 (purpose, scope, applicability).
Note the stack: Security Regulations, then S17, then G3, then practice guides, then local B/D policy.
Identify contacts: DITSO, IT Security Management Unit, ISIRT Commander, and your line manager.
Locate the local IT security policy and end-user instructions. G3 Appendix A is only a sample shape.
Confirm the current local policy links, including version and date.
Memorise the modality words: Shall, Should, and May (S17/G3 §4.2).
Skim S17/G3 §5: ISMC, ITSWG, GIRO, GovCERT.HK, and your departmental structure.
Find your role in G3 §5.2–5.3 and tick the duties that apply to you.
Write a one-page who-to-call card.
Read S17/G3 §6: CIA, risk-based decisions, security-by-design, and prevent / detect / respond / recover.
Write one sentence each for confidentiality, integrity, and availability on a system you use.
List two or three pain points (audit, near-miss, or App C doubts) to carry into the role path.
S17/G3 §7 management responsibilities, including the overview of risk and classified protection.
items.note: New joiners: all. Current staff: if gap.

items.text: S17/G3 §8 IT security policies. Departmental policy aligns with S17 and G3.
items.note: New joiners: all. Current staff: if gap.

items.text: S17/G3 §9 human resource security: joiners, leavers, and awareness.
items.note: New joiners: read carefully. Current staff: if gap.

items.text: Know your B/D security awareness and training requirement.
items.note: Current staff: if this day is a gap.

items.text: S17/G3 §10 asset management: ownership, classification, and media.
S17/G3 §11 access control at a high level: least privilege, passwords, mobile and remote access, IoT.
Practice: list assets you handle and their classification. Ask the Information Owner if you are unsure.
Skim S17/G3 §14 (malware, backup, logging, vulnerabilities, threats). Depth comes in the role path.
S17/G3 §18 incident management: how to report. Do not wait until you are sure.
S17/G3 §19 continuity: plans exist. Note where your B/D keeps them.
Save ISIRT and incident contacts on your who-to-call card.
S17/G3 §20 compliance: security risk assessment, audit, and technical review, at awareness level.
Learn Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 (G3 §4.1). Tier 2 and Tier 3 also take Appendix C.
Note which of your systems might be Tier 2 or Tier 3. Confirm that on the tier-mapping block. Do not self-finalise the tier.
Foundation refresh done. Continue the role path with your gap list.

roles.title: Elevated end user / general IT with elevated duties
roles.anchor: G3 §5 theme, plus admin tasks you actually hold
roles.quick: One-page personal SOP: login, classify, share, report.
roles.walk: Tabletop a security event on the ISIRT path, or a joiner/leaver check for an elevated account.

items.text: Read S17, then G3 §11: user responsibilities, passwords, and mobile or remote access.
Confirm elevated accounts are still justified, and that MFA is used where it is required.
Review the local acceptable-use rules and end-user instructions.
Read S17/G3 §10 on assets you create or handle.
Apply classification labels on documents you create.
Follow media, USB, and disposal rules.

clusters.focus: Cryptography and physical security, light pass

items.text: High-level pass of S17/G3 §12: when encryption is required.
S17/G3 §13: clear desk, clear screen, and secure areas.
S17/G3 §14.2–14.4 themes: malware, backup, and logging, at user level.
Act on patch prompts, suspicious mail, and USB discipline.
Know the backup expectation for data you own.
S17/G3 §15.2: classified transfer, email, and external parties.
Practice: encrypt, mark, and choose the channel the way local rules require.

clusters.order: S17 §18 → G3 §18, and §9 if you supervise others

items.text: Dry-run S17/G3 §18 reporting. Use a tabletop, not a fabricated live incident.
If you supervise temps or contractors, refresh §9 on leavers and transfers.

clusters.order: S17 §20 → G3 §20 → App C access control if Tier 2/3

items.text: Elevated access may be audited (§20, and App C access checks where Tier 2 applies).
If you are admin-adjacent to a Tier 2 or Tier 3 system, read the App C access-control bullets.

roles.title: System / LAN administrator
roles.quick: Privileged-account and patch-SLA one-pager for one production system.
roles.walk: Patch or vulnerability handling for one host, or privileged access from request to grant to review.

clusters.order: S17 §11 → G3 §11 → App C §11 if Tier 2/3

items.text: Read S17, then G3 §11 in full for administration, not only end-user duties.
Build or refresh the privileged-account inventory for systems you run.
Apply the strong-password expectation and MFA where it is required.
App C §11: an independent privileged-account check at least every six months, and MFA for interactive privileged logon where feasible.

clusters.order: S17 §14 → G3 §14 → App C §14 if Tier 2/3

items.text: Read S17, then G3 §14.
Malware protection on servers, not only on workstations.
Backups: local and off-site.
Logging that you can actually use in an incident.
Hardening and change control.
Patch and vulnerability process, including who is told if a fix slips.
App C §14: off-site backup, a capacity plan, an end-of-support migration plan at least six months ahead, and patching typically within a month, with DITSO visibility if it slips.
Tier 3 only: 24×7 monitoring of a SIEM class, drawing on more than one source.
items.note: Tier 3 only, on top of the Tier 2 App C controls.

clusters.order: S17 §15 → G3 §15, with G3 §11.5 for admin access

items.text: Read S17, then G3 §15.
Segmentation, gateway, wireless, and Internet-facing exposure.
Admin jump hosts and remote desktop inside the rules of G3 §11.5.
S17/G3 §13: equipment and secure areas you rely on.
S17/G3 §12: cryptography in transit and at rest for data you administer.
If a vendor runs the system or it sits in a cloud, read S17/G3 §17.
items.note: Skip the deep read only when no provider is in the path. Record that.

items.text: Write the shared-responsibility split in one paragraph: what you still own, and what the provider owns.
§18 runbook: how this system is reported and who is on the 7×24 path.
§19 contingency touchpoints for the system.
§20 vulnerability-scan and penetration-test cadence.
App C §19–20 for Tier 2/3: tested contingency, and the scan and pen-test expectations.
Current staff: map each App C control you touch to evidence or a gap.

roles.title: Application developer / maintenance
roles.quick: Put a security-requirements checklist into your SDLC template.
roles.walk: Security requirement, then a design note, then a test case. Or a test-data protection check.

items.text: S17 then G3 §16.1: security-by-design, specifications, secure coding, and testing.
App C §16: shift-left, a pre-production security risk assessment that checks design-review follow-ups, and hardening before the production baseline.
G3 §16.2: secure environment, source control, change control, and integrity.
Segregation: development administration is not production administration where that split is required.
G3 §16.3: protect production-like data and anonymise it where the rule requires.
S17/G3 §11.4 application access control.
§12 cryptography at rest and in transit.
Session handling, authentication, authorisation, and secrets. Secrets do not live in source.
§14.6 technical vulnerabilities for your stack, including libraries.
Logging under §14.4: what the app must emit for an incident.
§17 if the product is SaaS or built by a contractor.
Know that contracts carry security clauses. Point to the owner of those clauses.

clusters.order: S17 §18 → G3 §18, then §20, then App C if Tier 2/3

items.text: §18: what a secure-coding incident teaches, and how you would report one.
§20: security risk assessment, penetration test, and code review in the assurance path.
Tier 2/3: walk the App C development and compliance rows for your system.

roles.title: IT security administrator / unit
roles.quick: A living dashboard: privileged-review dates, patch-SLA breaches, open SRA items, and App C evidence links.
roles.walk: A privileged-account review sample, or an alert-to-triage-to-escalate drill.

items.text: Read the mandate in G3 §5.3.1 and the security-unit role in §5.2.5.
The security administrator should not be the same person as the system administrator.
Protect audit-log integrity. Reviewers should not be able to quietly rewrite the record.

clusters.order: S17 §11 → G3 §11 → App C §11 if Tier 2/3

items.text: S17/G3 §11 end to end, from join to review to removal.
Privilege reviews and joiner-mover-leaver.
App C §11: independent privileged-account audits for Tier 2 and Tier 3.
S17/G3 §14.2, 14.4, 14.6, and 14.7: malware, logging, vulnerabilities, and threats.
Patch governance: what “typically within a month” means, and when DITSO must see a delay.
Threat intelligence through GIRO and GovCERT.HK.
Tier 3 monitoring under App C §14: 24×7, multi-source, SIEM-class.
Review §15 and §12 with LAN administrators. Keep the segregation of duties intact.
§18 with the ISIRT: your part of detection, escalation, and the record.
§19: the security inputs a continuity plan needs.

clusters.order: S17 §20 → G3 §20 → App C §5 and §20, and App D when Tier 2/3

items.text: §20: security risk assessment, audit, and technical compliance.
G3 Appendix D when the system is Tier 2 or Tier 3. Learn what is submitted; do not invent a filing.
items.note: Applies when the tier is 2 or 3.

items.text: App C §5: a Tier 3 security unit has at least one member with a recognised certification.

roles.title: Management support (DITSO support)
roles.quick: A one-page B/D security governance map.
roles.effort: About 45–60 minutes a day. Oversight fluency, not deep admin how-to.
roles.walk: A management paper: draft tier inventory, top three risks, and an App C red/amber/green view.

clusters.order: S17 §5 → G3 §5.2 → App C §5 for Tier 3

items.text: S17/G3 §5.2.1: what the DITSO is accountable for.
§5.2.2 information security steering committee.
App C §5: a B/D with Tier 3 systems shall have a steering committee, and at least one certified member in the security unit.

clusters.order: S17 §7 → G3 §7 → App B, and App C §7 for Tier 3

items.text: §7 risk management and who owns the tier decision.
Use G3 Appendix B as guidance when someone proposes a tier. You still confirm with the owner.
Tier 3 risk registers under App C §7: risks, likelihood, severity, mitigation, and monitoring.

clusters.order: S17 §8 → G3 §8, and S17 §9 → G3 §9 → App C §9 for Tier 3

items.text: §8: is departmental policy current and aligned?
§9 training and awareness coverage.
App C §9: Tier 3 structured training, including vendors where feasible, or a contractual training duty.

clusters.order: Executive skim of §11 and §14, plus App C

items.text: Executive skim of §11 and §14 plus App C. Ask the unit for a red/amber/green view, not for packet captures.
§18 reporting path toward the Director and GIRO. Know who speaks externally.
§19: plans are tested, not only filed.

clusters.order: S17 §20 → G3 §20, and Appendix D for Tier 2/3

items.text: §20 security risk assessment and audit cadence.
Appendix D submissions for Tier 2 and Tier 3. Know that they exist and who files them.
Check awareness coverage: who has not had the required training.
One decision to prepare: fund or fix the top residual risk. Bring evidence, not a slogan.
List the systems and services you own, administer, develop, or heavily use.
Propose Tier 1, 2, or 3 using G3 §4.1 and Appendix B: impact, interdependency, and essential services.
Confirm the proposal with the Information Owner or the DITSO unit. Do not self-finalise Tier 2 or Tier 3.
Mark every Tier 2 or Tier 3 row: App C applies. Tier 3 includes every Tier 2 App C control, plus the Tier 3-only rows.

apply.label: Days 25–27
apply.title: App C and local-policy gap pass

items.text: If any system is Tier 2 or 3, walk G3 Appendix C for the sections you touch: §5, 7, 9, 11, 14, 16, 19, and 20.
Fill a gap table: Control, Evidence, Gap, Owner, Due.
Re-read the local B/D policy and note any rule that is stricter than S17/G3.
Attach audit or security-risk-assessment finding identifiers you already have.
If nothing is Tier 2 or 3: do the local-policy pass and a Tier 1 self-check on one system.
Document the steps and the artefacts you kept. An informal note is enough. This hub does not collect it.
Note any Shall you met and any Should you deferred, and why.
Optional: tick foundation, role, and apply self-progress, or note deferrals with dates.
Keep for yourself: the tier-list draft, the App C gap table if you have one, the walkthrough note, and the who-to-call card.
Current staff: you may share the gap table with your line manager or security unit so remediation owners can be booked.
items.note: Optional handoff. Not a mandatory acknowledgement.

items.text: Optional: skim one practice guide for your role on ITG InfoStation.
